Isolated showers tonight across Guam and Rota are expected to 
continue for the whole forecast period with the exception of 
scattered island effect showers in the afternoon Wednesday. For the 
Tinian and Saipan, a trough will continue to move through the region
and bring scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms tonight,
becoming isolated Wednesday. Showers will likely remain isolated 
until Friday when scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms return 
upon the passage of Typhoon In-fa somewhere to the north through the
far northern CNMI anywhere from just north of Saipan to Maug island.
Showers for Tinian and Saipan will likely return to isolated for the
rest of the forecast period by Saturday. Current Typhoon In-Fa is 
expected to make it's closest point of approach sometime Friday. 
Breezy conditions can be expected for Tinian and Saipan Friday with 
sustained winds up to 30 mph and gusts to 45 mph. The current JTWC 
track puts only a 10-20% chance of tropical storm sustained winds for
Tinian and Saipan. This situation remains highly uncertain and will 
continue to be monitored closely for any potential changes. See the 
"Tropical Systems" section for more details.

Marine...
Gentle northeast winds will prevail across Tinian and Saipan 
through at least Wednesday night, while mostly light winds prevail
over Rota and Guam. Scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms 
will be possible for Tinian and Saipan tonight as a trough moves 
through the region, with isolated thunderstorms possible for all
islands Wednesday. Therefore, there is a moderate risk of lightning
along the coastlines tonight for Tinian and Saipan, and all islands 
Wednesday. There will be a moderate risk of rip currents all week for north- 
and east-facing reefs due to a primary east-northeast swell and a 
secondary west-northwest swell that will become negligible by 
Wednesday. Combined seas are expected to waver between 5 and 6 feet 
through Thursday. By late Thursday, seas are expected to increase 
significantly and become hazardous ahead of Typhoon In-Fa that is 
anticipated to pass somewhere through the far northern CNMI between 
just north of Saipan to Maug island. Widespread seas of 10 to 15 feet
are expected for Tinian and Saipan with seas potentially up to 20 
feet possible if In-fa takes a more southern track. Seas of 10+ feet
are also possible for Guam and Rota. Therefore, the surf will also be
hazardous on all islands, particularity for north and east facing
reefs.

Tropical Systems...
At 1 PM ChST, Typhoon In-fa was located 205 miles north of Enewetak,
about 1265 miles east of Guam, near 14N162E. In-fa is nearly 
stationary, moving west at only 1 mph. Maximum sustained winds were 
125 mph. TY In-fa is expected to move west through Thursday, then 
begin to turn west-northwest by Friday, heading toward the island of 
Pagan in the far northern CNMI. In-fa is expected to weaken slightly 
through tonight, then begin to strengthen again Wednesday. TY In-fa 
could become a Super Typhoon as early as Thursday, and reach the 
northern CNMI at that intensity Friday afternoon. Residents of 
Tinian, Saipan and the far northern CNMI should continue to monitor 
forecasts for any updates or changes and the possibility of any 
watches or warnings, as changes in intensity, track and timing will 
occur over the next few days. A significant shift south could bring 
TC conditions to Tinian and Saipan, though this is not expected at 
this time.

For more information on TY In-fa, see bulletins issued by the Joint 
Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN31 PGTW and by the 
National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ31 PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
A fairly dry pattern is in store for eastern Micronesia through the
weekend. Mostly clear skies are expected at Majuro and Kosrae 
tonight, continuing at Kosrae through Wednesday night. The most that 
can be expected for Pohnpei and Kosrae is only isolated showers 
through the weekend. For Majuro, the monsoon trough looks to drift 
west over the next couple days, with a band of weak convergence 
setting up briefly over Majuro. This is expected to bring scattered 
showers to the atoll Wednesday through Wednesday night. By Thursday,
the dry pattern looks to return to Majuro.

For the marine forecast, nothing has really changed. Still looks like
combined seas at or below 6 feet through the weekend. Gentle to
moderate winds at Pohnpei will subside to light to gentle by
Thursday, while light to gentle winds will prevail at Kosrae and
Majuro through the weekend.

Western Micronesia...
